title: Someone Shouted
text:
Someone shouted:

Long live freedom!

and blood answered.


Someone shouted:

Death to the tyrant!,

and blood answered.


Tomorrow, blood will shout:

Long live freedom!

Death to the tyrant!,

and the people

will answer!
editorial_note: The translation keeps Soler's call-and-response structure, where blood first answers and then becomes the revolutionary voice.

title: My Homeland
text:
Paraguay

so many years loving you

became a habit in me.

You are tenacious in me

like the thrust

of the spring shoot

that is always latent

beneath winter

until the time arrives

that inexorably arrives

one day.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the homeland as a latent spring force waiting beneath political winter.

title: From Mocking Death So Much...
text:
From mocking death so much,

his blood was black.

From mocking the day so much,

his soul was black.

From mocking the people so much,

his life was black.

They simply

killed him.

At the place they found

only a black pit.

There was no one to ask.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated blackening and blunt, public erasure of the tyrant figure.

title: Thread of Sun
text:
I do not know by what

miracle of reflections

a little thread of sun

stealthily

passes every day

in a slight triangle

through the roof

of my cell.

I wait for it

I spy on it anxiously

I follow it and see it off

with sadness.

But at once I think:

tomorrow it will return

if they do not arrest it.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the fragile prison-light image and the final personification of the sun as another possible detainee.

title: Decrees
text:
It is forbidden

for hunger to eat

for the mouth to speak

for the ear to hear

for thirst to drink

for fire to warm

for fear to run

for cold to shiver

for joy to laugh

for love to love

for the poet to sing

for the wounded to moan

for spring to bloom

for gunpowder to explode.


Afterward

they shot them for not complying.


THE END




Chile, 1973
editorial_note: The translation keeps the authoritarian proclamation pattern and the absurdity of punishing natural forces for disobedience.
